=== README.md ===
# Deploying `slng` to SLNG

Unmute wrote the files in this directory and stopped. It opens no connection to
SLNG at any point, so nothing here has been pushed, checked against your
account, or reserved. The `voiceai` CLI does that part.

Everything in this directory is disposable. Edit the package and compile again.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `agent.json` | the agent create body |
| `tools/check_order.json` | a tool create body |
| `tools/refund.json` | a tool create body |
| `README.md` | this file |

The agent deploys to region **eu-central**.

## 1. Create these Vault entries first

SLNG reads these from its own secret store. Unmute knows the names and can
create none of them, and it has never seen a value: no secret value appears in
any file in this directory or on any command line below.

Create each one in the SLNG dashboard before you push. A name is an uppercase name starting with a letter, such as ACME_API_KEY, at most 64 characters.

**Secrets** — credentials a tool authenticates with.

| Vault name | Needed because |
|---|---|
| `REFUND_API_TOKEN` | tools/refund.yaml authenticates with it |

**Variables** — values SLNG substitutes into text at run time, written in the
package as `{{$NAME}}` tokens. Nothing declares them in the package: SLNG
holds the value, so only a slng target resolves one.

| Vault name | Needed because |
|---|---|
| `ACME_BRAND` | conversation.greeting.text |


## 2. Push the agent

The push tool reads its credential from `VOICEAI_API_KEY`. Export it once, or
run `voiceai login` and let the CLI store it:

```bash
export VOICEAI_API_KEY=...
```

That is **not** `SLNG_API_KEY`. `SLNG_API_KEY` is the Context Router's
key, which a generated livekit or pipecat project reads at run time. This target
generates no project and needs no such key. The two are different keys for
different things, and using one where the other belongs returns an
authentication error that looks like a wrong body.

Then push:

```bash
voiceai agents create --file build/slng/agent.json --json
```

An agent id comes back, and you need it for step 3. Keep it, or find it again
with `voiceai agents list`: unmute stores no id, writes no lockfile, and keeps
no local state about your account.

### Read this before you run that command

**This body is not postable exactly as written, and the command above will fail
on it.** `agent.json` carries a name in every place the API wants an identifier,
because no compiler can invent an id a server assigns.

Concretely: each entry under `tool_refs` is written as `{"tool": "<name>", ...}`,
and the API wants `attachment_id`, `tool_id` and `version`, all three required,
with no `tool` field at all. `mcp_refs` is the same shape. So a name has to
become an id before this file is accepted.

**A curated capability is no exception.** A builtin such as `end_call` is a tool
your organisation already owns, so it has a `tool_id` and that id still has to be
filled in. It needs nothing *created*, which is a smaller job, but it is not a
skipped one.

This package's curated references: `end_call`.

These tools need a body created first, then their new ids filled in:

- `tools/check_order.json`
- `tools/refund.json`

Each MCP reference is incomplete in a way that id resolution alone cannot fix.
SLNG requires a schema hash computed over the tool's input and output schemas
**as the live server reports them**, so the push step has to **connect to the
MCP server** before the reference can be completed. It is not a lookup.

- internal_docs · search_docs
- internal_docs · read_doc

The `voiceai` CLI has no `tools` command yet, so there is nothing that does this
for you today. Doing it by hand takes one edit per reference. Replace

```json
{ "tool": "check_order", "description": "...", "invocation": "model", "argument_overrides": {} }
```

with

```json
{
  "attachment_id": "0ad3148c-a454-4759-90b4-7941668278ad",
  "tool_id": "fd25f5c5-15e7-4662-b11b-62b82beba14c",
  "version": 3,
  "description": "...",
  "invocation": "model",
  "argument_overrides": {}
}
```

Keep the `description`, `invocation`, `argument_overrides` and any
`execution_policy` or `config_overrides` unmute wrote: those are the fields it
derived from your package, and they are correct. Only the three ids are yours to
supply.

- `tool_id` and `version` come from the tool itself. The quickest way to read
  them for a curated capability is `voiceai agents get <id> --json` on any agent
  that already has it attached: its `tool_refs` carry both.
- `attachment_id` is a fresh UUID that you mint. It identifies this attachment,
  not the tool, so it must not be copied from another agent.

Or post an agent with no tools at all, which needs none of this, and attach them
in the dashboard afterwards.

## 3. Talk to it

Use the agent id step 2 returned. It is not optional: the command creates a
session for one named agent.

The `--file` is not optional either, even though everything in it is. Write a
`session.json`:

```json
{"arguments": {}, "participant_name": "you"}
```

`arguments` is where this agent's variables get their value for one session. It
takes strings only, at most 32 of them.

This agent declares: `customer_id`, `customer_name`.
Leave one out and its declared default is used.

```bash
voiceai agents web-sessions create <agent_id> --file session.json
```

That returns LiveKit connection details, and dispatches a worker: a
`livekit_dispatch_id` in the response means the agent joined the room. Sessions
cap at `max_session_seconds`, which the same response carries.

There is no `unmute dev` for this target. `dev` runs the generated project
locally, and this target generates no project: SLNG runs the agent. The web
session above is how you talk to it.

## If the agent answers with silence

A model can pass every check at create time and still fail on the call. The
create body is validated against what your organisation is *allowed* to use;
whether the provider behind it actually answers is a different question, and
nothing in this directory can tell you.

The call record is where that shows up:

```bash
voiceai agents calls list <agent_id> --json
```

Read `call_end_reason` on the most recent entry. A line like

```text
terminal failure: component=llm reason=hard_fail
```

names the layer that failed: `llm`, `stt` or `tts`. That is a model or a
provider problem, not a problem with the body unmute wrote, and swapping that
one binding is the fix. A short `call_duration_ms` with the agent never speaking
is the same story.

## Before you download an agent and try to push it back

An agent document exported from the SLNG dashboard is **not** always a body the
API will accept. The export is a different shape from the create body, and the
differences bite:

- the export carries `orchestrator`, which the create body forbids outright. An
  export from an agent running on LiveKit omits the field at its default and
  posts cleanly; the same export from a Pipecat agent carries
  `orchestrator: "pipecat"` and is rejected.
- the export carries `idle_nudges`, `tools: []`, and null timeout fields the
  create body treats differently.
- `llm_router_enabled` defaults to `false` on the export and `true` on the
  create body, so a field omitted from one means the opposite in the other.

Compile from the package instead. That is the shape this file is.

## What unmute did not write, and why

- **No `orchestrator`.** It exists only on the exported document shape. SLNG
  runs each agent on LiveKit or Pipecat and chooses which itself.
- **No `idle_nudges`.** SLNG's idle handling needs three spoken texts a package
  does not carry. Leaving the field out lets SLNG apply its own defaults; a
  package that sets `conversation.inactivity` is refused at validate rather than
  having its setting quietly dropped.
- **No trunk or phone number.** Those are account state you make in the SLNG
  dashboard. Unmute buys no numbers and provisions no carrier state.
- **No inbound or outbound greeting.** Both need a telephony connection unmute
  does not create.
- **No `llm_router_enabled`.** SLNG decides. The field is left out so the
  platform applies its own default, the same way an agent made in the dashboard
  gets it, because nothing in a package describes SLNG's server-side routing.

  This matters more than it looks. A model your organisation brought its own key
  for has no entry in SLNG's shared catalogue, and SLNG accepts one **only** when
  the router is on. Writing the field off would refuse those models. Leaving it
  out lets them work.

- **Dependencies as written, canonicalised.** A code tool's `dependencies:` are
  emitted lowercase, dash-separated and sorted, because SLNG canonicalises the
  list it is given and stores the result. A body that carried the spelling you
  typed would not be the body that exists once it lands.

  Each is an exact `name==version` pin. A range is refused at validate: SLNG
  builds a locked, hash-verified environment per tool, and a range cannot be
  locked. The sandbox runs Python 3.14 and has `pydantic` already, so a handler
  that needs only the standard library and pydantic pins nothing.

- **No model checking.** Model strings are forwarded exactly as written, because
  SLNG owns its own model list and unmute keeps no copy of it. The compile report
  above names every binding it forwarded.

  So this is the field most likely to fail your push, and it fails loudly:
  `AGENT_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`, naming `models.stt`, `models.llm` or `models.tts`
  and the string it rejected. Three different things cause it:

  - the model is not enabled for agents in your organisation;
  - it is one of your own models and SLNG's router is off;
  - it is not served in the region and language this agent asked for. Not every
    model exists in every region. `deployment_region: any` avoids this by letting
    SLNG route each call, which is why it is worth trying before you pin one.
=== agent.json ===
{
  "schema_version": 2,
  "name": "slng",
  "system_prompt": "You are the front desk for Acme Support.\n\nAnswer in one or two short sentences. Use the caller's name once, near the\nstart, and not again.\n\nIf the caller says they are finished, or says goodbye, end the call.\n",
  "greeting": "Hi {{customer_name}}, you have reached {{$ACME_BRAND}} support.",
  "language": "en",
  "region": "eu-central",
  "models": {
    "stt": "slng/deepgram/nova:3-en",
    "llm": "openai/gpt-5.6-luna",
    "tts": "slng/deepgram/aura:2-en",
    "tts_voice": "aura-2-thalia-en",
    "stt_kwargs": {},
    "llm_kwargs": {
      "temperature": 0.4
    },
    "tts_kwargs": {}
  },
  "enable_interruptions": true,
  "tool_mode": "shared",
  "tool_refs": [
    {
      "tool": "check_order",
      "description": "Look up an order by its id and return its status and delivery date.",
      "invocation": "model",
      "execution_policy": {
        "pre_action_message": {
          "enabled": true,
          "text": {
            "segments": [
              {
                "type": "literal",
                "value": "One moment while I look that up."
              }
            ]
          },
          "wait": false
        }
      },
      "argument_overrides": {}
    },
    {
      "tool": "refund",
      "description": "Start a refund for the caller's order.",
      "invocation": "model",
      "argument_overrides": {
        "channel": "voice"
      },
      "config_overrides": {
        "type": "api_request",
        "url": "https://api.acme.example/refunds/{{customer_id}}"
      }
    },
    {
      "tool": "end_call",
      "description": "End the call when the caller is finished or says goodbye.",
      "invocation": "model",
      "argument_overrides": {}
    }
  ],
  "mcp_refs": [
    {
      "server": "internal_docs",
      "tool_name": "search_docs",
      "invocation": "model"
    },
    {
      "server": "internal_docs",
      "tool_name": "read_doc",
      "invocation": "model"
    }
  ],
  "runtime_variables": [],
  "template_defaults": {
    "customer_id": "unknown",
    "customer_name": "there"
  },
  "template_variable_options": {
    "customer_id": {
      "required": true
    },
    "customer_name": {
      "required": true
    }
  }
}
=== tools/check_order.json ===
{
  "name": "check_order",
  "description": "Look up an order by its id and return its status and delivery date.",
  "tool_type": "code",
  "config": {
    "import_probes": [],
    "egress": {}
  },
  "code_src": "\"\"\"The author's own handler, and the slng driver copies this text unchanged.\n\nThat is what keeps one file working on all three targets: LiveKit and Pipecat\nimport it and call the function, and SLNG introspects the Input and Output\nclasses the driver appends below it.\n\"\"\"\n\nORDERS = {\n    \"A1\": {\"status\": \"shipped\", \"delivers_on\": \"2026-09-01\"},\n}\n\n\ndef check_order(order_id: str) -> dict:\n    return ORDERS.get(order_id, {\"status\": \"unknown\", \"delivers_on\": \"\"})\n\n\n# Generated by unmute. SLNG derives this tool's parameter and result\n# schemas by introspecting Input and Output, and calls handler().\n# Everything above this line is your own handler file, unchanged.\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel\n\n\nclass Input(BaseModel):\n    order_id: str\n\n\nclass Output(BaseModel):\n    delivers_on: str | None = None\n    status: str | None = None\n\n\ndef handler(input: Input) -> Output:\n    result = check_order(order_id=input.order_id)\n    return Output(**result)\n",
  "declared_secrets": [],
  "dependencies": [
    "orjson==3.11.4",
    "pydantic-core==2.41.5"
  ]
}
=== tools/refund.json ===
{
  "name": "refund",
  "description": "Start a refund for the caller's order.",
  "tool_type": "api_request",
  "config": {
    "url": "https://api.acme.example",
    "http_method": "POST",
    "auth": {
      "type": "bearer",
      "secret_name": "REFUND_API_TOKEN"
    },
    "headers": [],
    "parameters": {
      "properties": {
        "reason": {
          "description": "Why the caller wants a refund",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "timeout_seconds": 10,
    "wait_for_response": true
  }
}
